I have 19.1 mu total. I split it into two parts: 15.1 mu for wheat-maize double cropping, and 4 mu for cotton. I have done it this way for many years. My son and daughter-in-law work in Shijiazhuang, so I only have my wife and myself for daily work. Four mu of cotton is enough—any more and I would need to hire too many pickers in the autumn.

For the wheat, I planted Shixin 828 last October. It is an improved variety, and my neighbor Lao Zhang uses it every year. Last fall I put down one bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu—50 kg each mu. This spring, at green-up time, I will top dress with 40 jin of urea per mu, which is 20 kg. That gives me about 16 kg of pure nitrogen per mu in total. I will irrigate three times from my well: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at heading. Two pesticide sprays—one for weeds and one at heading for insects and disease. If the weather is normal, I should harvest 550 kg per mu in early June.

For the maize, after wheat harvest I will plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed. Everyone in our village plants this because it is reliable. I direct seed into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. We only have three or four days between wheat harvest and maize planting, so there is no time to plow. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then top dress with 25 kg of urea per mu when the plants are knee-high. That is about 17 kg nitrogen per mu. I will irrigate twice: once at jointing in July, and once at tasseling in early August. Two pesticide applications. I expect 650 kg per mu.

For the cotton, I will plant hybrid Bt cotton on 4 mu in late April. I rotary till in spring first. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, plus I add extra potassium because cotton loves it—15 kg of potassium sulfate per mu. At flowering I top dress with 15 kg urea per mu. That comes to about 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs more care: I will irrigate three times and spray pesticide four times. Even Bt cotton gets aphids and mites. I hope for 320 kg per mu of seed cotton.

I do not cut fertilizer to save money. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. But I do not go crazy either. I watch what my neighbors do. Last year I used about the same amounts, and I will do the same this year. Change is risky.
